detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Install and configure the required add-on or app: EHR SSO logs, IdP.
• Ensure the following data sources are available: `sourcetype="epic:login"`, `sourcetype="okta:systemlog"`.
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Step-up auth from new countries; peer-group baseline per department; VIP patient list access rules.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
index=healthcare sourcetype="epic:login" outcome="success"
| iplocation src
| stats dc(Country) as countries, count by user_id
| where countries>2 OR count>100
| sort -count
```

Understanding this SPL

**EHR Login Anomaly Detection** — Unusual geography, time, or volume of EHR logins may indicate credential theft or insider snooping.

Documented **Data sources**: `sourcetype="epic:login"`, `sourcetype="okta:systemlog"`. **App/TA** (typical add-on context): EHR SSO logs, IdP. The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

The first pipeline stage scopes events using **index**: healthcare; **sourcetype**: epic:login. That sourcetype matches what this use case lists under Data sources.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Scopes the data: index=healthcare, sourcetype="epic:login". Cross-check against **Data sources** above so indexes and sourcetypes match your ingestion.
• Pipeline stage (see **EHR Login Anomaly Detection**): iplocation src
• `stats` rolls up events into metrics; results are split **by user_id** so each row reflects one combination of those dimensions.
• Filters the current rows with `where countries>2 OR count>100` — typically the threshold or rule expression for this monitoring goal.
• Orders rows with `sort` — combine with `head`/`tail` for top-N patterns.


Step 3 — Validate
Run the search on recent production data, spot-check a handful of results against the source system or operational runbooks (cash operations, EHR, payment gateway, etc.), and adjust thresholds to match your seasonal patterns and test windows so teams are not flooded with noise.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Add the search to a dashboard or set up alert actions (email, webhook, PagerDuty, etc.) as required. Document the use case in your runbook and assign an owner. Consider visualizations: Map (logins), Table (risky users), Timeline (session starts).

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (EHR SSO logs, IdP — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=epic:login into healthcare. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`countries, user_id`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: In Healthcare, we pay close attention to "EHR Login Anomaly Detection" in our day-to-day work so that fraud, waste, and compliance issues do not slip by quietly. We help teams focus on the few situations that need a person, not every routine blip in the data.
